incidents.victim: Apollo Global Management (and other financial firms)
incidents.vector: Attackers impersonated IT support in voice-phishing and social-engineering calls to gain access to the firm's cloud platforms between July 6 and July 10.
incidents.impact: Names, dates of birth, home addresses and Social Security numbers were compromised; Apollo is the first to confirm data theft in an extortion wave (attributed by Google to the group operating as BlackFile/The Com under brands Redact, Pink, Helix and Falcon) that also targeted competitors including Blackstone and Bain Capital.

incidents.victim: U.S. Bancorp (via third/fourth-party contractor)
incidents.vector: A ransomware crew (operating as LockBit) claimed the bank as a victim; U.S. Bancorp traced the claim to a breach at a contractor of a third party, outside its own environment.
incidents.impact: The bank, the 7th largest in the U.S., says there is no evidence its systems, networks or data repositories were compromised; the group provided no data samples and threatened to leak within two weeks.

incidents.victim: Hospital for Sick Children (SickKids), Canada
incidents.vector: Data theft tied to a third-party software application briefly took down the hospital's careers website.
incidents.impact: Personal information of current and former employees, job applicants and staff of related organizations including the SickKids Foundation was likely stolen; no clinical systems or patient data were involved. Affected people were offered two years of credit monitoring.

incidents.victim: Open-source software ecosystem (npm packages incl. keyv, cacheable)
incidents.vector: A self-propagating worm (ChainDrop) used malicious npm preinstall scripts to launch an obfuscated payload that read live process memory on GitHub Actions runners to steal OIDC tokens and credentials, then republished additional infected packages.
incidents.impact: Over 400 packages including massively popular libraries were hijacked; the worm harvested cloud secrets, backdoored local developer tools (VS Code, Claude Code) and used Ethereum blockchain transactions for command-and-control.

incidents.victim: Government bodies across Central Asia
incidents.vector: Spear-phishing with region-tailored Office documents, sometimes in password-protected RAR archives, triggered macros deploying seven RAT families (five previously undocumented) for long-term access.
incidents.impact: A China-nexus operation (SilkParasite, linked to FamousSparrow) targeted government entities in Uzbekistan, Turkmenistan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Kazakhstan; the modular, AI-assisted toolset routes command traffic over trusted services like Google Drive to evade detection.

incidents.victim: Internet-exposed web servers worldwide (government, education, media, technology, gaming)
incidents.vector: The group exploited publicly disclosed one-day vulnerabilities (Zimbra, Nacos, AjaxPro and Linux privilege-escalation flaws) to gain remote code execution, then used agentic AI to automate reconnaissance, exploit refinement and persistence.
incidents.impact: A Chinese-speaking crime group (UAT-10147) compromised servers across Brazil, Bolivia, China, Canada and Vietnam for SEO fraud and data theft, deploying the new cross-platform SPECTRE implant with a Linux rootkit and bring-your-own-vulnerable-driver capability to blind EDR tools; a target list of ~170,000 URLs was recovered.

incidents.victim: Microolap (Russian network-monitoring software firm)
incidents.vector: A group calling itself Black Spark claimed a month-long intrusion; the company says attackers reached only rarely used legacy development systems, an outdated website and an old Bitrix24 CRM with limited data.
incidents.impact: Hackers claimed they extracted and deleted data belonging to major Russian customers (Russian Railways, Goznak, VTB Bank, NEK.TECH) and accessed the EtherSensor traffic-analysis platform; Microolap denies its core infrastructure or customer data was compromised.

incidents.victim: Rust developer ecosystem (arrayref and two other crates)
incidents.vector: Attackers compromised a popular Rust developer's account and injected malware into three libraries; infrastructure overlaps with prior North Korean operations per Wiz.
incidents.impact: The malicious versions were live for only 23 minutes, but one affected library (arrayref) has nearly 5 million weekly downloads; the Rust security team removed the packages and locked the account.

incidents.victim: U.S. critical infrastructure operators using Siemens S7 PLCs
incidents.industry: Critical infrastructure / manufacturing, energy, water, chemical
incidents.vector: Threat actors use internet scanning to find exposed or poorly protected Siemens S7 PLCs and deploy AI-generated Python exploit scripts (built on snap7 libraries) disguised as legitimate monitoring tools to gain read/write access via the S7comm protocol.
incidents.impact: CISA, NSA, FBI, DOE and EPA warned of an active threat conducting reconnaissance and capability development against S7-200/300/400/1200/1500 controllers, assessed as pre-positioning for future operational effects against Critical Manufacturing, Energy, Water, Chemical, Food/Agriculture and Commercial Facilities.

incidents.victim: CareCloud (electronic health records provider)
incidents.vector: A March 2026 cybersecurity incident exposed personal data held by the electronic health records company.
incidents.impact: CareCloud disclosed that 3.7 million people were affected by the breach.

incidents.victim: Latvia road traffic safety directorate (CSDD)
incidents.vector: Hackers stole personal data from the country's road traffic agency.
incidents.impact: Personal information, payment receipts and license-plate details of 1.2 million Latvian citizens dating to 2008 were stolen; the CSDD leadership resigned and authorities warned citizens of follow-on scams.

incidents.victim: U.S. government agencies and universities
incidents.vector: A long-running intrusion campaign targeting government agencies and academic institutions to steal research and credentials.
incidents.impact: U.S. federal authorities re-upped charges against alleged Iranian hackers tied to the Mabna Institute for a sprawling hacking campaign against government agencies and universities.

incidents.victim: Multiple large enterprises (incl. McDonald's, Vodafone, Kyndryl, Gap, hotel chains)
incidents.vector: An actor using the handle 'TheHatman' claims to have used compromised credentials, MFA fatigue and password spraying to access victims' Microsoft Entra (Azure) tenants; the specific intrusion vector is unverified.
incidents.impact: The actor posted across forums from Aug 1-17 offering to sell employee data allegedly exfiltrated from the Entra tenants of nearly a dozen high-profile organizations, including McDonald's, Vodafone, Kyndryl, Gap and the Intercontinental and Wyndham hotel chains.

incidents.victim: Organizations running Fortinet, Sophos and MSSQL edge devices
incidents.vector: A large-scale, internet-wide password-spraying campaign ('FortiBleed') uses a curated password list against internet-exposed services, then extracts device configuration files and cracks stored credentials offline to establish persistent administrator access.
incidents.impact: An initial access broker on a Russian-language forum claimed responsibility and offered harvested credentials for sale; the multi-stage campaign builds an ever-growing credential list reused against new targets. Palo Alto Networks shared findings with the Cyber Threat Alliance.

incidents.victim: Companies hiring remote technical staff (1,100+ targeted)
incidents.vector: Operators (PurpleDelta), likely based in China, maintain fabricated personas backed by AI-generated photos, custom ChatGPT assistants and forged identity documents to secure remote jobs, using real-time AI transcription during interviews.
incidents.impact: At least 22 personas applied to over 1,100 companies and were likely employed at ten or more organizations, creating insider-threat exposure; earnings are funneled to fund North Korea's sanctioned military and nuclear programs.

incidents.victim: Global organizations across critical infrastructure sectors
incidents.vector: The Medusa ransomware-as-a-service recruits initial access brokers and exploits unpatched internet-facing software (ScreenConnect, Fortinet, Fortra GoAnywhere, BeyondTrust), often weaponizing new CVEs within 24 hours.
incidents.impact: CISA, FBI and HHS updated their advisory reporting Medusa actors have now impacted over 500 victims across critical infrastructure sectors using a double-extortion model.

incidents.victim: University of Texas at San Antonio
incidents.vector: A security breach over the weekend forced the university to take IT systems offline.
incidents.impact: The university took systems offline, extended tuition payment deadlines and planned to reset all account passwords once systems were restored; classes were expected to start as scheduled.

incidents.victim: Winnipeg Health Sciences Centre
incidents.vector: A ransomware attack disabled the hospital's access-card door system and building controls.
incidents.impact: Access doors and heating, ventilation and air conditioning were disabled at Winnipeg's largest hospital, prompting increased on-site security; the hospital said patient care and clinical operations were not impacted.

incidents.victim: Slovakia national traffic-camera network
incidents.vector: Slovakia's NBU found that NERO R-ONE traffic cameras — a rebranded Russian CORDON PRO.M model bought via a Cyprus shell company — contain a backdoor that executes code delivered by SMS from hardcoded Russian phone numbers.
incidents.impact: 279 cameras were installed nationwide under a EUR 30 million EU-funded project; the devices also had Secure Boot disabled, a vulnerable web portal and unauthenticated live streams. Deployment was paused pending an independent audit.

incidents.victim: Baylor Genetics
incidents.vector: A June 2026 security breach exposed personal information of patients and employees.
incidents.impact: Compromised data included medical testing information, laboratory test results, health insurance information and Social Security numbers; the company did not disclose the number of affected individuals.

incidents.victim: Berlin city government (transport and urban development departments)
incidents.vector: A cyberattack disrupted email, remote gateways and internet connectivity across two major city departments.
incidents.impact: IT staff disconnected the transport and urban development departments from the city network to contain the incident; no attribution was provided.

incidents.victim: Bluesky and GitHub
incidents.vector: Distributed denial-of-service attacks flooded the platforms with junk traffic over roughly 24-hour periods.
incidents.impact: An Iranian hacktivist group known as the 313 Team took credit for prolonged outages at Bluesky (Sunday) and GitHub (Monday); Bluesky said it upgraded its defenses in response.

incidents.victim: Government networks in Taiwan and Thailand
incidents.vector: Suspected Chinese hackers used publicly available AI tools, chaining Hermes and OpenClaw agents to automate reconnaissance, initial access, lateral movement and data exfiltration.
incidents.impact: Attackers breached Taiwanese government networks and Thailand's Ministry of Finance as part of a wave of AI-assisted intrusions across Asian governments; described as among the first near-autonomous AI attacks on government targets.

incidents.victim: CEVA Logistics (and downstream customers across Europe)
incidents.vector: Hackers gained access to the French shipping and logistics company's systems and began leaking customer data on the dark web.
incidents.impact: The breach disrupted freight delivery across large parts of Europe; affected companies included Valve's Steam hardware business and Dutch retailers Bol and De Bijenkorf, with customers facing days- to weeks-long delivery delays.

incidents.victim: Government and critical-infrastructure organizations worldwide
incidents.vector: The Gunra ransomware-as-a-service (derived from leaked Conti source code) gains initial access primarily by exploiting known Fortinet FortiOS/FortiProxy authentication-bypass vulnerabilities and VPN gateway flaws, then uses double extortion.
incidents.impact: FBI, CISA, DC3, NSA, U.S. Secret Service and South Korea's KNPA issued a joint advisory on the emerging Gunra threat, which encrypts data and exfiltrates business-critical documents, databases and PII across victims in the Americas, Europe, Middle East, Africa and Asia-Pacific.

incidents.victim: WilmerHale and Goodwin Procter (U.S. law firms)
incidents.vector: A group (Luna Moth / Silent Ransom Group) that specializes in attacking law firms used voice phishing and social engineering to gain access.
incidents.impact: Two of the largest U.S. law firms paid multi-million-dollar ransoms this year — WilmerHale at least $18 million and Goodwin Procter $10 million.
